# I stopped running after ten years

From the spring I turned thirty-two, I woke at 5:30 every morning and ran five kilometres, in the rain and around hotels on business trips. It had become part of who I was. Last winter I stopped.

## My knee

It started with pain in my right knee. The orthopaedist said the meniscus was thinning and told me to run three times a week at most. Three times a week would have been enough, but I stopped entirely. Running every morning had become a rule, and skipping a single morning felt like it would break the rule.

## Evening walks

I began walking the dog for forty minutes each evening. At first it felt like something was missing, since I didn't get out of breath, didn't sweat and didn't feel I had achieved anything. Around the second week I noticed my mind was quieter on those walks; when I ran, I had only ever thought about pace and distance.

## What I liked

It seems what I liked was less the running than the time when I didn't have to talk to anyone. The morning half hour used to be that time, and now the evening forty minutes are.

My knee still aches a little. In spring I might try running again, twice a week and short distances at first, though not as a rule: only on the mornings I want to.
